name: What are the red flags that a bathroom addition will be too expensive?

mainEntity.name: What early signs tell you a bathroom addition may have hidden cost problems?
mainEntity.text: What early signs tell you a bathroom addition may have hidden cost problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several early signs suggest a bathroom addition may become expensive. Long distances to existing plumbing, slab foundations, structural wall changes, and outdated electrical systems can all raise cost quickly. Another warning sign is a layout that requires moving multiple wet areas instead of keeping the new bathroom near existing utility lines. If the contractor’s quote is vague, missing permit costs, or light on waterproofing details, that is another red flag. Bathroom additions can hide surprises behind walls and floors, so a realistic plan should assume some contingency. The best way to avoid a budget blowout is to identify the expensive conditions before demolition starts and simplify the design where possible. A smart layout often saves more money than trying to negotiate a cheaper labor rate.
acceptedAnswer.description: Warning signs include long plumbing runs, slab cutting, structural changes, outdated wiring, and a layout that requires moving multiple wet areas. If a quote is vague or excludes permits and waterproofing, the project may cost more than it first appears.
